title: Concordance chart & cycle handbook for reliability initiatives (SLO reconciliation, error budget tranches)
creator: Leah Chen
description:
Problem: Teams run independent SLOs and error budget policies which makes cross-team rollouts, incident-driven rollbacks, and quarterly planning unpredictable. We lack a single reconciliation view that shows: active SLO targets, current burn rates, tranche allocations, pending rollouts that consume budget, and where automated fallbacks exist.

Objective: Produce a Concordance Chart (visual matrix) and an accompanying Cycle Handbook that together: 1) reconcile SLI definitions across product areas, 2) map error budget tranches to OKR/initiative owners, 3) define cadence and triggers for tranche reallocation, and 4) provide a lightweight ops handoff for incident and postmortem workflows.

Scope: Focus on production-facing HTTP/text-generation APIs, Dedicated pools, and Console routes that directly affect latency and availability SLOs. Exclude internal infra-only SLIs (e.g., GPU health metrics) except where they cascade to customer-visible errors.

Deliverables:
- Concordance Chart (spreadsheet + embedded dashboard view) showing SLI name, SLI definition/source query, SLO threshold, burn-rate trend (7d, 30d), current tranche remaining, owning team, rollback policy link, and ticketed rollouts scheduled in the cycle.
- Cycle Handbook (markdown doc) with step-by-step process for: pre-cycle reconciliation, tranche allocation, mid-cycle review cadence, emergency tranche transfer, automated rollback policy template, and template PRD/incident link checklist.
- Two dashboards in Console: a compact "initiative-reliability heatmap" and an "error-budget manager" view to drive weekly ops standups.

Success metrics:
- 90% of active reliability initiatives adopt the handbook for next cycle's planning.
- Reduce cross-team error budget escalations that require exec intervention from average 3/month to <=1/month within two cycles.
- Time to rollback a rollout (when SLI breach occurs) reduced from median 28m to <=12m in integrated teams.

Out-of-scope: automatic enforcement of tranche transfers via RBAC; that will be a follow-up initiative (see dependencies).
acceptance_criteria: Concordance Chart populated with SLI/SLO mappings for at least 6 product areas: hosted-api, dedicated, private-console, embeddings, routing, and batching
Cycle Handbook reviewed and approved by Reliability, Platform, and Growth PMs (explicit sign-off recorded)
Heatmap dashboard implemented with drilldowns to SLO burn by team and annotated with active rollouts
Weekly ops playbook (2-page) created and validated in one live ops runbook rehearsal
Documentation links to PRDs and rollback runbooks are present in at least 80% of chart entries

comments: 2025-10-21: Discovery interviews completed with 9 teams. Found inconsistent SLI naming (latency_95 vs p95_latency) and differing windowing (5m vs 1h). Need a canonical naming appendix.
2025-11-12: Prototype chart shared. Feedback from Platform: prefer metric-source column that points to PromQL/ClickHouse queries. Action: add 'source query' column and sample query for each SLI.
2025-12-02: Workshop with Serving Runtime. Decision: treat KV-cache eviction latency as a dependent SLI but do not own tranche allocation; reference only. Marco to own mapping changes.
2026-01-21: Dashboard PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/reliability-dashboards/pull/47. Waiting on ENG-9321 to merge to enable burn-rate series.
2026-02-02: Legal reviewed handbook for customer-data links and requested redaction guidelines for screenshots. Handbook updated with redaction checklist.

2026-02-23: Pilot scheduled for 2026-W09 with Dedicated and Hosted API teams. Ops rehearsal booked for 2026-03-08. Note: Need one more on-call runbook owner for Europe region (assigned to Priya tentatively).
notes:
Trade-offs discussed: 1) Tightening SLO windows increases noise and false positives — handbook recommends 3-tier windowing (5m for alerting, 1h for operational, 7d for planning). 2) Automating tranche transfers requires RBAC + billing changes; postpone to post-pilot. 

Next steps: finish data plumbing for burn-rate metrics (ENG-9321 owner), finalize canonical SLI appendix, and run the ops rehearsal on 2026-03-08.
